newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Directionless amid US holiday.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Directionless amid US holiday.

text.p: The Singapore oil product swaps market was largely steady in thin discussions due to the Thanksgiving holiday in the U.S., market sources said on Thursday.
"It is typical behaviour for the market because of the holiday," said a trader.
But some traders said they expected some activity later as traders emerge from the Singapore physical market later on Thursday.
Even a physical trade of 220,000 barrels of gas oil late Wednesday evening at a high of $31.80 a barrel free-on-board Singapore, lifting mid-December, was unable to shift the market.
"It is high enough for the market," said a trader on the deal level.
December gas oil swaps was last quoted at $31.30/$31.55, unchanged from $31.30.$31.45 on Wednesday.
The gas oil had already risen sharply over the past few days due to renewed buying interest by traders in Singapore for spot prompt cargoes with demand still outstanding in China, traders said.
But the arbitrage window for western exports into Asia was closed as demand was restricted to prompt deliveries which traders said was too soon to ship cargoes.
The backwardation on paper between December and January was at least $1.00 per barrel, brokers said.
The December/Janaury backwardation is at a steep $1.00/$1.10 which makes arbitrage exports for the further out months, they said.
The jet fuel/gas oil spread (regrade) was steady with the December regrade offered at $1.90, and January at $1.80.
With lack of firm direction from crude, December naphtha was unchanged at $23.55/$23.80 and fuel oil at $118.50/$119.50.
